1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons; and wherein the weapons stores processor panel is configured to receive and process interlock signals from at least one external avionics system prior to enabling firing of the aircraft weapons.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard; and wherein the weapons stores processor panel further communicates with the flight management system via a MIL-STD-1553 avionics interface bus.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons processor panel; wherein the laser pointer is independently controlled by the weapons stores processor panel separate from the weapons interface fire signal generation.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display; wherein the data concentrator unit is configured to format display information according to a predetermined display protocol.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display; wherein the display information is selectively routed based on operational mode of the weapons stores processor panel.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons; wherein the weapons stores processor panel generates firing command sequences that are transmitted to the weapons bus controller only when all safety interlocks are satisfied.
